stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that \( x'(t) = 4 e^{\frac{t}{3}} \sin{\left(t \right)} \) and \( y(t) = - 2 t + 3 \ln{\left(t^{2} + 1 \right)} \) for \( t \ge 0 \). Using a calculator, find \( x''(\frac{3}{2}) \) and \( y''(\frac{3}{2}) \), the components of the acceleration of the particle at \( t = \frac{3}{2} \). Show the setup for the calculations, and give each value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The component given as a velocity is differentiated once, \( \frac{4 e^{\frac{t}{3}} \sin{\left(t \right)}}{3} + 4 e^{\frac{t}{3}} \cos{\left(t \right)} \) at \( t = \frac{3}{2} \) gives about 2.659.
The component given as a position is differentiated twice, \( - \frac{6 \left(t - 1\right) \left(t + 1\right)}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{2}} \) at \( t = \frac{3}{2} \) gives about -0.710.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative of a position component

worked_solution.text: The acceleration at \( t = \frac{3}{2} \) is \( x''(\frac{3}{2}) \approx 2.659 \) and \( y''(\frac{3}{2}) \approx -0.710 \).

options.label: \( x''(\frac{3}{2}) \approx -0.710 \) and \( y''(\frac{3}{2}) \approx 2.659 \)
options.derivation: the two components written in the wrong order

options.label: \( x''(\frac{3}{2}) \approx 2.659 \) and \( y''(\frac{3}{2}) \approx 0.769 \)
options.derivation: each given component differentiated once, so the position component yields its velocity, not its acceleration
